intro: Hip pain can make everyday things like walking, climbing stairs or getting comfortable in bed feel difficult, and it is easy to put off finding help. Searching for hip pain physiotherapy near you is a sensible step towards understanding what is going on and what you can do about it. We can introduce you to a UK physiotherapist who works with hip pain, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for hip pain physiotherapy usually need
need_lead: Most people typing this search want a local physiotherapist who understands hip pain and can help them move more comfortably.
needs: You have pain on the outside of your hip that is worse when lying on that side or when walking, and you want to know how to settle it.
You have been told you have hip arthritis and want exercise and activity advice to keep moving.
You feel pain in the groin or front of the hip when walking, turning or getting out of a chair, and it is not easing.
You are recovering from hip surgery and need rehabilitation close to home.
You are unsure whether your hip pain needs a physiotherapist at all and want to talk it through with someone qualified.
context_heading: Checking that your physiotherapist is registered
context: Physiotherapist and physical therapist are protected titles in the UK, so anyone using them must be registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). You can check the HCPC register online before you book. Most physiotherapists are also members of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy, shown by the letters MCSP.

Sports therapists, massage therapists and personal trainers can be helpful for some needs, but they are not physiotherapists. For hip pain, particularly after surgery or if you have another health condition, check that the person you see is an HCPC-registered physiotherapist.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Describe where the hip pain is and whether it is on the outside, in the groin or at the front of the hip.
Say how long the pain has been there and whether it started suddenly or came on gradually.
Mention what makes it worse, such as walking, stairs, lying on that side or getting out of a chair.
Tell us whether you have a diagnosis such as hip arthritis or have had hip surgery.
Let us know your postcode or the area you would like the physiotherapist to be near.
Mention any other health conditions or mobility needs that the physiotherapist should know about.
questions: Are you registered with the HCPC, and what is your registration number?
How will you assess my hip pain and what will the first appointment involve?
Will you give me exercises and activity advice I can do at home?
What should I do about sleep if lying on my sore hip is uncomfortable?
How will we know whether the physiotherapy is helping?
What will it cost, and how many appointments might I need?

faqs.a: Exercise and activity advice are widely used to help people with hip arthritis stay active and manage their symptoms. A physiotherapist can help you find movement that suits your hip and your daily life.

faqs.q: Why does my hip hurt more when I lie on it?
faqs.a: Pain on the outside of the hip is often linked to the tendons in that area, and pressure from lying on that side can make it sore. A physiotherapist can talk through sleep positions and loading exercises that may help.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral from my GP?
faqs.a: You can usually approach a physiotherapist directly, though some clinics may ask about your GP or medical history. It is worth mentioning any diagnosis or surgery when you enquire.

faqs.q: How do I know the physiotherapist is qualified?
faqs.a: Physiotherapist is a protected title in the UK, so anyone using it must be registered with the HCPC. You can check the HCPC register online, and many physiotherapists also hold MCSP membership.
